rules.name: A small opposing wick with a large body supports expansion in the candle direction
rules.setupAnchor: Measure the candle body and the wick opposite the candle direction after the candle closes
rules.confirmationTrigger: Bullish expansion support appears when the lower wick is small and the candle closes near its high; bearish expansion support appears when the upper wick is small and the candle closes near its low
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: A candle that supports expansion provides the directional context for later protected swings and continuation entries in the same direction
rules.invalidationCondition: The opposing wick consumes too much of the candle's range or the close finishes too close to the open instead of the directional extreme
rules.targetLogic: When the candle supports expansion, prioritize continuation targets such as external liquidity or average range objectives rather than the opening price
exceptions: A small same-side wick does not invalidate the candle; the key measurement is the wick opposing the intended expansion
machineChecks: Compute the wick opposite the candle direction and compare it against the body
Require the close to finish near the directional extreme rather than near the open
Classify the candle as expansion-supporting only when the opposing wick remains small relative to the full range
ambiguityNotes: The first numeric threshold for what counts as a small opposing run is not yet fixed

rules.name: A large opposing wick with a smaller body favors reversion toward the open or nearby liquidity
rules.setupAnchor: Identify candles where most of the range was consumed by the wick opposite the intended expansion direction
rules.confirmationTrigger: Treat the candle as reversal-leaning when the opposing wick dominates the candle anatomy and the close finishes closer to the open than the directional extreme
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Large rejection wicks warn that continuation structure is weak and protected swings in the candle direction are less likely to hold cleanly
rules.invalidationCondition: The next candle immediately reasserts directional expansion with a small opposing wick and closes beyond the rejection range
rules.targetLogic: Favor targets back toward the opening price or nearby liquidity instead of expecting a large directional expansion from the same candle
exceptions: Large-wick reversal candles can still lead to continuation later, but usually after the next candle or a later confirmation step rather than immediately
machineChecks: Classify candles with dominant opposing wicks as poor expansion candidates
Downgrade continuation expectations when the close finishes too close to the open
Switch the target model toward the open or nearby liquidity after a large opposing run
ambiguityNotes: The exact cutoff for when the wick dominates enough to invalidate expansion still needs a stricter algorithm

rules.name: Respect or disrespect of the wick midpoint determines whether rejection is holding or failing
rules.setupAnchor: Measure the wick from the body edge to the wick extreme and mark its 50 percent midpoint
rules.confirmationTrigger: If price respects the midpoint, expect continuation opposite the wick; if price closes through the midpoint, treat the wick as disrespected and expect continuation in the original direction of the wick
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: A respected wick midpoint helps validate the reversal structure that later protected swings should build from
rules.invalidationCondition: Price closes through the midpoint and proves the wick rejection did not hold
rules.targetLogic: Use midpoint respect as the hold/fail filter before deciding whether to follow the wick-based reversal or abandon it
exceptions: Do not prioritize midpoint logic for internal-range wicks that did not sweep a meaningful level or reach a clear point of interest
machineChecks: Compute the wick midpoint from the body edge to the wick extreme
Track whether subsequent closes remain on the respected side of the midpoint
Flip the wick state from respected to disrespected once a close breaches the midpoint

rules.name: Higher-timeframe wick behavior should govern whether lower-timeframe structure is read as expansion, reversal, or range
rules.setupAnchor: Start from the higher-timeframe candle, then evaluate the lower-timeframe setup in the context of that parent wick behavior
rules.confirmationTrigger: A shallow opposing run on the higher timeframe supports lower-timeframe expansion, while a large opposing run suggests lower-timeframe reversal setups or range-bound expectations
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Lower-timeframe protected swings are higher quality when they agree with the higher-timeframe wick read instead of fighting it
rules.invalidationCondition: The lower-timeframe setup assumes expansion even though the higher-timeframe candle is printing a large opposing wick or other clear rejection behavior
rules.targetLogic: Use the higher-timeframe wick read to choose between continuation targets, reversal targets, or more conservative range expectations on the lower timeframe
exceptions: Lower timeframes can still move against the higher-timeframe wick read, but those moves should be treated as lower-quality or counter-context
machineChecks: Classify the higher-timeframe candle first as expansion-supporting or reversal-leaning based on wick behavior
Gate lower-timeframe expansion reads on the higher-timeframe wick classification
Downgrade lower-timeframe continuation setups when the parent candle shows large opposing rejection
ambiguityNotes: The strict minimum mismatch needed before a lower-timeframe setup should be rejected instead of merely downgraded still needs a formal rule
